# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

```dart
if (result.exitCode != 0) {
 throw StateError(

``

This does NOT include the stderr tail. The reviewer says the live shape has `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` on stderr (exit 154). To classify this shape, the write error should include the stderr tail — the reads already do `_errorTail`. So the fix for thread 3:

1. In `secure_key_store_io.dart` `write()`: include the stderr tail in the error message, like reads do: `'security add-generic-password failed (exit ${result.exitCode}): ${result.stderr}'` when stderr is non-empty. This makes the "authorization was canceled" tail reach the diagnostic.
2. Extend `isMissingDefaultKeychainError` to also match `authorization was canceled` (and maybe the SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent shape). The reviewer suggested `contains('authorization was canceled')`.

Hmm, but wait — should I be careful about Windows Credential Locker / Linux writing errors containing "authorization was canceled"? Unlikely shapes. The classification is macOS-oriented anyway ("default keychain" language in advisory). The repair flow only makes sense on macOS. The wizard calls `_offerDefaultKeychainRepair` which runs `security default-keychain -s ...` — on a non-macOS host this fails and prints "could not run the repair command". Since classification only happens when the diagnostic matches, and "authorization was canceled" would only come from macOS security CLI (exit 154), that's fine.

Also the preflight shape: `'no default keychain (exit N)'`.

Now, the reviewer's option 1 wording: "Also classify the add-generic-password failure tail (e.g. contains('authorization was canceled')) — or better, have the write preflight run security default-keychain classification for that error too, since it is the same root cause."

I'll implement:
- `isMissingDefaultKeychainError` matches both shapes: `no default keychain` OR `authorization was canceled`.
- Include stderr tail in the add-generic-password write failure so the canceled shape is actually classifiable.

Tests:
- Test in secure_key_store_test.dart that a failed `add-generic-password` (exit 154 with stderr tail) surfaces the tail in the thrown error (via SecureKeyCache.save → saveFailureDiagnostic contains 'authorization was canceled').
- Test that `isMissingDefaultKeychainError` classifies the canceled shape.
- Wizard-level test: store fails with canceled-authorization diagnostic → advisory + repair offer shown. And repair-success + retry-failure prints the loud line (not mute).

## PR Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \
  test/cli/provider_wizard_loud_save_test.dart \
  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \
  test/model_roles/provider_key_resolver_store_health_test.dart
dart analyze lib bin
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[wizard key step] --> P[_persistSetupKey]
  P -->|save true| E[entry + key, byte-identical]
  P -->|save false| L[LOUD line: slot + label + diagnostic]
  L --> D{missing default keychain?}
  D -->|yes| O["[y/N] repair offer — runs only on y, then re-saves"]
  D -->|no| F[entry recorded with keyNotPersisted flag]
  O -->|n| F
  B[boot] --> N[secureKeySaveDegradationLines]
  N -->|flagged entry, empty slot| BL["one line per slot + retry command (stderr)"]
  H[no-key hint / 401] --> S{store degraded?}
  S -->|yes| HW["secure store not writable (diagnostic) … /key set"]
  S -->|no| HP["no key set; store one with /key set"]
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no-token edit silently clears the `keyNotPersisted` marker**

`entry.keyNotPersisted = keyNotPersisted;` overwrites the marker unconditionally, but `_persistSetupKey` returns `keyNotPersisted: false` in its **no-fresh-token edit branch** (`provider_key_persist.dart:36-40`):

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted: false,   // ← not "persisted", just "not attempted"
  );
}
```

Failure scenario on an incident-shaped host (store still unwritable, slot still empty):

1. Wizard add of `kimi_ira` → write fails → entry recorded with `keyNotPersisted: true` — every boot prints the degradation note (working as designed).
2. The user runs `/provider` edit on the entry and changes only the model, leaving the key prompt empty (a normal, store-independent edit).
3. The marker is cleared even though no save was attempted, let alone successful. The yaml persists without the flag and the cross-boot degradation note disappears — the silent-keyless-boot symptom this card set out to kill can return through an unrelated edit.

This contradicts the field's own contract in `custom_providers.dart`: *"Cleared by a later successful save of [keyName]"* — and AC1's "the next boot shows the degradation note" promise.

Suggested fix: in the no-token edit branch, carry the existing marker over instead of resetting it:

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted:
        editName != null
            ? (registry?.find(editName)?.keyNotPersisted ?? false)
            : false,
  );
}
```

(Heads-up: `mergeEditedCustomProviderEntry` also rebuilds the entry from scratch and relies on this assignment line to set the flag — the same carry-over covers the rename path.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: boot degradation note prints before `migrateLegacyKeySlots` can fill the slot**

This loop is placed **before** the gh-1570 legacy-slot migration a few lines below (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart:651-683`), while `secureKeySaveDegradationLines` decides "slot still empty" via the preload snapshot (`keys.read(keyName) != null`).

If a flagged entry's canonical slot is empty but a legacy cross-spelling slot holds the key, the migration copies it onto the canonical slot **right after** this warning prints — so the boot emits a "key did not reach the store" line for a slot that is populated one statement later. Rare (needs a `keyNotPersisted` entry whose key actually lives under a legacy spelling), but it produces exactly the kind of self-contradicting output this card removes elsewhere.

Cheap fix: run the degradation-line loop **after** the `migrateLegacyKeySlots` block (the migration itself writes through `keyCache`, so the `keys.read` skip would then see the copied slot and stay silent). No test change expected — the boot test drives the pure function directly.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the repair offer covers only the preflight failure shape — the incident's second live shape gets no remedy**

`isMissingDefaultKeychainError` matches only the write **preflight** string (`'no default keychain'`, thrown at `secure_key_store_io.dart:282`). That path correctly gets the loud failure line (E2's requirement) but never the `[y/N]` repair offer, even though the underlying host defect (no default keychain pointer) is the same one the remedy fixes.

Two small options, either fine:

1. Also classify the `add-generic-password` failure tail (e.g. `contains('authorization was canceled')`) — or better, have the write preflight run `security default-keychain` classification for that error too, since it is the same root cause.
2. Leave as-is for this card, but note in the advisory that a canceled keychain dialog points at the same remedy.

Secondary nit in the same block: when the repair command succeeds (`repaired == true`) but the **retried** save fails again (`await keys.save(...)` → false), the flow falls through to `return (keyName: keyName, keyNotPersisted: true)` **without printing anything** — the user just saw "default keychain restored — retrying the save" and then silence. Add a loud line on that second failure (the same wording as the first) so the retry outcome is never mute.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the degraded hint names the suggested slot but a diagnostic from a possibly different slot**

`degradedStoreHint` keys on the **global** `keys.saveFailures` counter and renders `keys.lastSaveError` — the last failure of *any* slot. If `FA_KEY_A`'s save failed and the user then hits a no-key state on an unrelated `FA_KEY_B`, the hint reads:

Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1691
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1691
- **Title**: gh-1679 [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1679` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1063
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T12:52:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T12:55:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \
  test/cli/provider_wizard_loud_save_test.dart \
  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \
  test/model_roles/provider_key_resolver_store_health_test.dart
dart analyze lib bin
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[wizard key step] --> P[_persistSetupKey]
  P -->|save true| E[entry + key, byte-identical]
  P -->|save false| L[LOUD line: slot + label + diagnostic]
  L --> D{missing default keychain?}
  D -->|yes| O["[y/N] repair offer — runs only on y, then re-saves"]
  D -->|no| F[entry recorded with keyNotPersisted flag]
  O -->|n| F
  B[boot] --> N[secureKeySaveDegradationLines]
  N -->|flagged entry, empty slot| BL["one line per slot + retry command (stderr)"]
  H[no-key hint / 401] --> S{store degraded?}
  S -->|yes| HW["secure store not writable (diagnostic) … /key set"]
  S -->|no| HP["no key set; store one with /key set"]
```

</details>

# pr-1691: gh-1679 [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \
  test/cli/provider_wizard_loud_save_test.dart \
  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \
  test/model_roles/provider_key_resolver_store_health_test.dart
dart analyze lib bin
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[wizard key step] --> P[_persistSetupKey]
  P -->|save true| E[entry + key, byte-identical]
  P -->|save false| L[LOUD line: slot + label + diagnostic]
  L --> D{missing default keychain?}
  D -->|yes| O["[y/N] repair offer — runs only on y, then re-saves"]
  D -->|no| F[entry recorded with keyNotPersisted flag]
  O -->|n| F
  B[boot] --> N[secureKeySaveDegradationLines]
  N -->|flagged entry, empty slot| BL["one line per slot + retry command (stderr)"]
  H[no-key hint / 401] --> S{store degraded?}
  S -->|yes| HW["secure store not writable (diagnostic) … /key set"]
  S -->|no| HP["no key set; store one with /key set"]
```

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1691
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1691
- **Title**: gh-1679 [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1679` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1063
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T12:52:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T12:55:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \
  test/cli/provider_wizard_loud_save_test.dart \
  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \
  test/model_roles/provider_key_resolver_store_health_test.dart
dart analyze lib bin
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[wizard key step] --> P[_persistSetupKey]
  P -->|save true| E[entry + key, byte-identical]

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1691._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart` line 391

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no-token edit silently clears the `keyNotPersisted` marker**

`entry.keyNotPersisted = keyNotPersisted;` overwrites the marker unconditionally, but `_persistSetupKey` returns `keyNotPersisted: false` in its **no-fresh-token edit branch** (`provider_key_persist.dart:36-40`):

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted: false,   // ← not "persisted", just "not attempted"
  );
}
```

Failure scenario on an incident-shaped host (store still unwritable, slot still empty):

1. Wizard add of `kimi_ira` → write fails → entry recorded with `keyNotPersisted: true` — every boot prints the degradation note (working as designed).
2. The user runs `/provider` edit on the entry and changes only the model, leaving the key prompt empty (a normal, store-independent edit).
3. The marker is cleared even though no save was attempted, let alone successful. The yaml persists without the flag and the cross-boot degradation note disappears — the silent-keyless-boot symptom this card set out to kill can return through an unrelated edit.

This contradicts the field's own contract in `custom_providers.dart`: *"Cleared by a later successful save of [keyName]"* — and AC1's "the next boot shows the degradation note" promise.

Suggested fix: in the no-token edit branch, carry the existing marker over instead of resetting it:

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted:
        editName != null
            ? (registry?.find(editName)?.keyNotPersisted ?? false)
            : false,
  );
}
```

### Thread 2 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` line 657

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: boot degradation note prints before `migrateLegacyKeySlots` can fill the slot**

This loop is placed **before** the gh-1570 legacy-slot migration a few lines below (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart:651-683`), while `secureKeySaveDegradationLines` decides "slot still empty" via the preload snapshot (`keys.read(keyName) != null`).

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart` line 81

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the repair offer covers only the preflight failure shape — the incident's second live shape gets no remedy**

`isMissingDefaultKeychainError` matches only the write **preflight** string (`'no default keychain'`, thrown at `secure_key_store_io.dart:282`). 1. Also classify the `add-generic-password` failure tail (e.g. `contains('authorization was canceled')`) — or better, have the write preflight run `security default-keychain` classification for that error too, since it is the same root cause.
2. Leave as-is for this card, but note in the advisory that a canceled keychain dialog points at the same remedy.

Add a loud line on that second failure (the same wording as the first) so the retry outcome is never mute.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/key_status.dart` line 392

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the degraded hint names the suggested slot but a diagnostic from a possibly different slot**

`degradedStoreHint` keys on the **global** `keys.saveFailures` counter and renders `keys.lastSaveError` — the last failure of *any* slot. If `FA_KEY_A`'s save failed and the user then hits a no-key state on an unrelated `FA_KEY_B`, the hint reads:

```

  and keys pasted earlier may not have persisted — fix the store, then

```

Slot and diagnostic can disagree, which is a smaller version of the "practically a lie" problem this card fixes. The per-name data to do better is already there (`failedSaveNames` / `saveFailureDiagnostic`). Options:

- Or keep the aggregate wording but say "last write failure" instead of implying the diagnostic belongs to `suggested`'s slot.

Same consideration applies to the `HostKeyResolver._missingKeyHint` degraded branch (it receives `lastStoreError` with no slot context). Behavior is defensible as-is (store health *is* global), so this is polish, not a defect.

# pr-1691: gh-1679 [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1691._

> ℹ️ **14 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart` line 391

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no-token edit silently clears the `keyNotPersisted` marker**

`entry.keyNotPersisted = keyNotPersisted;` overwrites the marker unconditionally, but `_persistSetupKey` returns `keyNotPersisted: false` in its **no-fresh-token edit branch** (`provider_key_persist.dart:36-40`):

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted: false,   // ← not "persisted", just "not attempted"
  );
}
```

Failure scenario on an incident-shaped host (store still unwritable, slot still empty):

1. Wizard add of `kimi_ira` → write fails → entry recorded with `keyNotPersisted: true` — every boot prints the degradation note (working as designed).
2. The user runs `/provider` edit on the entry and changes only the model, leaving the key prompt empty (a normal, store-independent edit).
3. The marker is cleared even though no save was attempted, let alone successful. The yaml persists without the flag and the cross-boot degradation note disappears — the silent-keyless-boot symptom this card set out to kill can return through an unrelated edit.

This contradicts the field's own contract in `custom_providers.dart`: *"Cleared by a later successful save of [keyName]"* — and AC1's "the next boot shows the degradation note" promise.

Suggested fix: in the no-token edit branch, carry the existing marker over instead of resetting it:

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted:
        editName != null
            ? (registry?.find(editName)?.keyNotPersisted ?? false)
            : false,
  );
}
```

(Heads-up: `mergeEditedCustomProviderEntry` also rebuilds the entry from scratch and relies on this assignment line to set the flag — the same carry-over covers the rename path.)

### Thread 2 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` line 657

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: boot degradation note prints before `migrateLegacyKeySlots` can fill the slot**

This loop is placed **before** the gh-1570 legacy-slot migration a few lines below (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart:651-683`), while `secureKeySaveDegradationLines` decides "slot still empty" via the preload snapshot (`keys.read(keyName) != null`).

If a flagged entry's canonical slot is empty but a legacy cross-spelling slot holds the key, the migration copies it onto the canonical slot **right after** this warning prints — so the boot emits a "key did not reach the store" line for a slot that is populated one statement later. Rare (needs a `keyNotPersisted` entry whose key actually lives under a legacy spelling), but it produces exactly the kind of self-contradicting output this card removes elsewhere.

Cheap fix: run the degradation-line loop **after** the `migrateLegacyKeySlots` block (the migration itself writes through `keyCache`, so the `keys.read` skip would then see the copied slot and stay silent). No test change expected — the boot test drives the pure function directly.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart` line 81

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the repair offer covers only the preflight failure shape — the incident's second live shape gets no remedy**

`isMissingDefaultKeychainError` matches only the write **preflight** string (`'no default keychain'`, thrown at `secure_key_store_io.dart:282`). The incident RCA (ticket, "Live evidence" #2) documents a second real shape on the same broken host: the actual `add-generic-password` failing with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceling the system "reset to default" dialog. That path correctly gets the loud failure line (E2's requirement) but never the `[y/N]` repair offer, even though the underlying host defect (no default keychain pointer) is the same one the remedy fixes.

Two small options, either fine:

1. Also classify the `add-generic-password` failure tail (e.g. `contains('authorization was canceled')`) — or better, have the write preflight run `security default-keychain` classification for that error too, since it is the same root cause.
2. Leave as-is for this card, but note in the advisory that a canceled keychain dialog points at the same remedy.

Secondary nit in the same block: when the repair command succeeds (`repaired == true`) but the **retried** save fails again (`await keys.save(...)` → false), the flow falls through to `return (keyName: keyName, keyNotPersisted: true)` **without printing anything** — the user just saw "default keychain restored — retrying the save" and then silence. Add a loud line on that second failure (the same wording as the first) so the retry outcome is never mute.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/key_status.dart` line 392

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the degraded hint names the suggested slot but a diagnostic from a possibly different slot**

`degradedStoreHint` keys on the **global** `keys.saveFailures` counter and renders `keys.lastSaveError` — the last failure of *any* slot. If `FA_KEY_A`'s save failed and the user then hits a no-key state on an unrelated `FA_KEY_B`, the hint reads:

```
— no key set; the secure store is not writable (<FA_KEY_A's diagnostic>)
  and keys pasted earlier may not have persisted — fix the store, then
  /key set FA_KEY_B <value>
```

Slot and diagnostic can disagree, which is a smaller version of the "practically a lie" problem this card fixes. The per-name data to do better is already there (`failedSaveNames` / `saveFailureDiagnostic`). Options:

- If exactly one name is degraded and it differs from `suggested`, mention it by name: `the secure store is not writable (last failure: FA_KEY_A — <diag>)`.
- Or keep the aggregate wording but say "last write failure" instead of implying the diagnostic belongs to `suggested`'s slot.

Same consideration applies to the `HostKeyResolver._missingKeyHint` degraded branch (it receives `lastStoreError` with no slot context). Behavior is defensible as-is (store health *is* global), so this is polish, not a defect.

# pr-1691: gh-1679 [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \
  test/cli/provider_wizard_loud_save_test.dart \
  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \
  test/model_roles/provider_key_resolver_store_health_test.dart
dart analyze lib bin
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[wizard key step] --> P[_persistSetupKey]
  P -->|save true| E[entry + key, byte-identical]
  P -->|save false| L[LOUD line: slot + label + diagnostic]
  L --> D{missing default keychain?}
  D -->|yes| O["[y/N] repair offer — runs only on y, then re-saves"]
  D -->|no| F[entry recorded with keyNotPersisted flag]
  O -->|n| F
  B[boot] --> N[secureKeySaveDegradationLines]
  N -->|flagged entry, empty slot| BL["one line per slot + retry command (stderr)"]
  H[no-key hint / 401] --> S{store degraded?}
  S -->|yes| HW["secure store not writable (diagnostic) … /key set"]
  S -->|no| HP["no key set; store one with /key set"]
```

</details>

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1691._

> ℹ️ **14 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart` line 391

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no-token edit silently clears the `keyNotPersisted` marker**

`entry.keyNotPersisted = keyNotPersisted;` overwrites the marker unconditionally, but `_persistSetupKey` returns `keyNotPersisted: false` in its **no-fresh-token edit branch** (`provider_key_persist.dart:36-40`):

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted: false,   // ← not "persisted", just "not attempted"
  );
}
```

Failure scenario on an incident-shaped host (store still unwritable, slot still empty):

1. Wizard add of `kimi_ira` → write fails → entry recorded with `keyNotPersisted: true` — every boot prints the degradation note (working as designed).
2. The user runs `/provider` edit on the entry and changes only the model, leaving the key prompt empty (a normal, store-independent edit).
3. The marker is cleared even though no save was attempted, let alone successful. The yaml persists without the flag and the cross-boot degradation note disappears — the silent-keyless-boot symptom this card set out to kill can return through an unrelated edit.

This contradicts the field's own contract in `custom_providers.dart`: *"Cleared by a later successful save of [keyName]"* — and AC1's "the next boot shows the degradation note" promise.

Suggested fix: in the no-token edit branch, carry the existing marker over instead of resetting it:

```dart
if (token == null) {
  return (
    keyName: editName != null ? registry?.find(editName)?.keyName : null,
    keyNotPersisted:
        editName != null
            ? (registry?.find(editName)?.keyNotPersisted ?? false)
            : false,
  );
}
```

(Heads-up: `mergeEditedCustomProviderEntry` also rebuilds the entry from scratch and relies on this assignment line to set the flag — the same carry-over covers the rename path.)

### Thread 2 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` line 657

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: boot degradation note prints before `migrateLegacyKeySlots` can fill the slot**

This loop is placed **before** the gh-1570 legacy-slot migration a few lines below (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart:651-683`), while `secureKeySaveDegradationLines` decides "slot still empty" via the preload snapshot (`keys.read(keyName) != null`).

Rare (needs a `keyNotPersisted` entry whose key actually lives under a legacy spelling), but it produces exactly the kind of self-contradicting output this card removes elsewhere.

Cheap fix: run the degradation-line loop **after** the `migrateLegacyKeySlots` block (the migration itself writes through `keyCache`, so the `keys.read` skip would then see the copied slot and stay silent). No test change expected — the boot test drives the pure function directly.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart` line 81

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the repair offer covers only the preflight failure shape — the incident's second live shape gets no remedy**

`isMissingDefaultKeychainError` matches only the write **preflight** string (`'no default keychain'`, thrown at `secure_key_store_io.dart:282`). The incident RCA (ticket, "Live evidence" #2) documents a second real shape on the same broken host: the actual `add-generic-password` failing with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceling the system "reset to default" dialog. That path correctly gets the loud failure line (E2's requirement) but never the `[y/N]` repair offer, even though the underlying host defect (no default keychain pointer) is the same one the remedy fixes.

Two small options, either fine:

1. Also classify the `add-generic-password` failure tail (e.g. `contains('authorization was canceled')`) — or better, have the write preflight run `security default-keychain` classification for that error too, since it is the same root cause.
2. Leave as-is for this card, but note in the advisory that a canceled keychain dialog points at the same remedy.

Secondary nit in the same block: when the repair command succeeds (`repaired == true`) but the **retried** save fails again (`await keys.save(...)` → false), the flow falls through to `return (keyName: keyName, keyNotPersisted: true)` **without printing anything** — the user just saw "default keychain restored — retrying the save" and then silence. Add a loud line on that second failure (the same wording as the first) so the retry outcome is never mute.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/key_status.dart` line 392

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the degraded hint names the suggested slot but a diagnostic from a possibly different slot**

`degradedStoreHint` keys on the **global** `keys.saveFailures` counter and renders `keys.lastSaveError` — the last failure of *any* slot. If `FA_KEY_A`'s save failed and the user then hits a no-key state on an unrelated `FA_KEY_B`, the hint reads:

```
— no key set; the secure store is not writable (<FA_KEY_A's diagnostic>)
  and keys pasted earlier may not have persisted — fix the store, then
  /key set FA_KEY_B <value>
```

Slot and diagnostic can disagree, which is a smaller version of the "practically a lie" problem this card fixes. The per-name data to do better is already there (`failedSaveNames` / `saveFailureDiagnostic`). Options:

- If exactly one name is degraded and it differs from `suggested`, mention it by name: `the secure store is not writable (last failure: FA_KEY_A — <diag>)`.
- Or keep the aggregate wording but say "last write failure" instead of implying the diagnostic belongs to `suggested`'s slot.

Same consideration applies to the `HostKeyResolver._missingKeyHint` degraded branch (it receives `lastStoreError` with no slot context). Behavior is defensible as-is (store health *is* global), so this is polish, not a defect.

# pr-1691: gh-1679 [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \
  test/cli/provider_wizard_loud_save_test.dart \
  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \
  test/model_roles/provider_key_resolver_store_health_test.dart
dart analyze lib bin
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[wizard key step] --> P[_persistSetupKey]
  P -->|save true| E[entry + key, byte-identical]
  P -->|save false| L[LOUD line: slot + label + diagnostic]
  L --> D{missing default keychain?}
  D -->|yes| O["[y/N] repair offer — runs only on y, then re-saves"]
  D -->|no| F[entry recorded with keyNotPersisted flag]
  O -->|n| F
  B[boot] --> N[secureKeySaveDegradationLines]
  N -->|flagged entry, empty slot| BL["one line per slot + retry command (stderr)"]
  H[no-key hint / 401] --> S{store degraded?}
  S -->|yes| HW["secure store not writable (diagnostic) … /key set"]
  S -->|no| HP["no key set; store one with /key set"]
```

</details>

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
